claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree T and original leaf v with support s, H=T-{v,s}, W=N_T(s)-{v}, and R=H-W satisfy alpha(H)=alpha(T)-1. At p=alpha(T)-2, q_v(j)=i_j(H)-i_j(R) counts independent j-sets of H meeting W, the target summand equals q_v(p)-q_v(p-1), the strict favorable selector equals Delta_p(H)+Delta_(p-1)(R)<0, and the aggregate is the resulting difference of tagged shell cardinalities. Per-leaf residuality holds exactly when alpha(R)<=alpha(T)-2; otherwise alpha(R)=alpha(T)-1.
claims.scope: Exact ordinary-tree coefficient and residual-split identities at p=alpha(T)-2, including zero-extended boundary ranks; no nonpositive aggregate theorem or injection follows.
claims.reason: A direct independent-set partition proves every identity, including the strict selector and distinct leaf tags. An independent closed-form calculation reproduces the eligible T_100 row. The T_22 mechanism obstructions cited in the origin report are at p=34 rather than that tree's frozen p=66, so they remain only mechanism fences.

claims.scope: One explicit eligible ordinary tree at its first interior rank; finite exact scope only, with both residual and non-residual selected tags.
claims.reason: Direct enumeration of all 4096 vertex subsets independently yields the polynomial, three maximum sets, strict selectors, local q counts, and the seven-tag complete sum; a hub-conditioned product formula checks the polynomial. The row probes the non-residual scope absent from T_m without refuting the aggregate sign.

limitations: The identity does not establish the selected tagged-shell cardinality comparison or the primary aggregate sign.
The independent numerical checks cover one order-403 family member and one 12-vertex mixed-regime tree, not an all-tree census.
